messages.subject: CFA difference in results between R and Mplus
parts:
Hello,

I am new to Lavaan and I am struggling to figure out what is causing a difference between my R and Mplus results. Can someone please help me understand why there would be differences between anayses for a 1 factor CFA? Most noticable differences on Chi Squared analysis and Number of Free Parameters, as well as RMSEA


My R syntax is as follows:

##CFA
library(naniar)
library(lavaan)
data = CFA_Random_Half_lifteime_3_2_20_without_cases_with_missing_on_all_variables_and_NA_replaced_for_R
Group1factor <- 'factor1=~ trafficr + carr + arrest + money + sch + scwrk + kids + rents + friend + pass + mem + broke + job'
fit1 <- cfa (Group1factor, ordered= c("trafficr", "carr", "arrest", "money", "sch", "scwrk", "kids", "rents", "friend", "pass", "mem", "broke", "job"),
             data = data)
            
summary(fit1, fit.measures = TRUE)
mi <- modindices(fit1, sort.=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: CFA difference in results between R and Mplus
parts: I think it is because you are not including  meanstructure = TRUE in the CFA command. Mplus includes the mean structure by default. If you put "MODEL=NOMEANSTRUCTURE;" in Mplus (if this is still an option) and run it you'll see the mean estimation of your 13 variables are the 13 degrees of freedom.

messages.subject: Re: CFA difference in results between R and Mplus
parts:
When using ordered items, lavaan will present more differences from Mplus. Lavaan can tell you which equations are being use to estimate these models, while Mplus differed even when they say (in their technical papers) that they use the same equations.
A while back Yves stop trying to match the Mplus output, as it becomes a tedious bactracking process of which changes Mplus is making to the original equations. And in lavaan we know exactly which equations are being used, so we are more confident on this\.
Mplus is famous for hidding parts of their process, to keep their software hard to replicate. But this ends in issues like this, as we are not clear what is going on under the hood

On Thursday, March 12, 2020 at 9:45:11 PM UTC-5, Scott Colwell wrote:
I think it is because you are not including  meanstructure = TRUE in the CFA command. Mplus includes the mean structure by default. If you put "MODEL=NOMEANSTRUCTURE;" in Mplus (if this is still an option) and run it you'll see the mean estimation of your 13 variables are the 13 degrees of freedom.

I think it is because you are not including  meanstructure = TRUE in the CFA command. Mplus includes the mean structure by default. If you put "MODEL=NOMEANSTRUCTURE;" in Mplus (if this is still an option) and run it you'll see the mean estimation of your 13 variables are the 13 degrees of freedom.

messages.subject: Re: CFA difference in results between R and Mplus
parts:
I believe that Mplus will -by default- constrain all factor loadings and
intercepts/thresholds to be equal across all groups, while lavaan only
does this if requested using eg group.equal = c("loadings", "thresholds").

In any case, you can check

lavInspect(fit1)

to see which parameters are free (or not), and you can compare this with
teh TECH1 output from Mplus.

Yves.
